issues.failure_explanation: In the determinant part of the proof, $\|D_x\tilde v^\theta({[\Phi_t^\theta]}^{-1}(x),1-t)-D_xu^\mu({[\Phi_t^\mu]}^{-1}(x),1-t)\|$ is bounded by $\sup_{(x,t)}\|D_x(\tilde v_t^\theta-u_t^\mu)(x)\|$, which is valid only when both derivatives are evaluated at the same point; but ${[\Phi_t^\theta]}^{-1}(x)\ne{[\Phi_t^\mu]}^{-1}(x)$ in general, since the two different vector fields induce different backward trajectories from the same $x$. The missing term is the spatial Lipschitz constant of $D_xu^\mu$ times the trajectory separation. Concrete failure of the inference: take $\tilde v^\theta=u^\mu+w$ with a small constant field $w$ (so the same-point bound is $0$) and $u^\mu$ with spatially varying derivative; the left side is then positive while the claimed bound is $0$.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add and subtract $D_xu^\mu({[\Phi_t^\theta]}^{-1}(x),1-t)$ and bound the spatial increment by $\operatorname{Lip}(D_xu^\mu)\le c_{d,k,\kappa,\mathcal{K}}$ (from $u^\mu\odiv\eta_d\in C^k$, $k\ge3$, uniformly over $\mathcal T$) times the Gronwall bound on $\|{[\Phi_t^\theta]}^{-1}(x)-{[\Phi_t^\mu]}^{-1}(x)\|$ already derived in the same proof; the extra term has the same form as the final KL estimate and is absorbed into its constant.
issues.overall_effect: The Jacobian-difference estimate, the determinant bound and hence the KL model-error bound of thm:learnability_target_class are not established as written; the model-error control inside the main theorem relies on this result.
issues.title: Model-error proof bounds a derivative difference at two distinct trajectory points by a same-point supremum
issues.why_classification: The repair is local, uses only ingredients already in the proof or cited in it, requires no new lemma, and preserves the statement and all rates; only an omitted term must be inserted and absorbed.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof claims, as a consequence of [Cor. 2.14, ipsen2008], that $|\log|\det A|-\log|\det B||\le\sum_{k=1}^d\binom{d}{k}2^k\|A-B\|^k$ for the inverse-flow Jacobians $A=D_x[\Phi^\theta]^{-1}(x)$, $B=D_x[\Phi^\mu]^{-1}(x)$. Such a bound cannot hold for general invertible matrices with a constant depending only on $d$: for $A=\epsilon I$, $B=2\epsilon I$ the left side equals $d\log 2$ while the right side tends to $0$ as $\epsilon\to0$. A correct log-determinant perturbation bound necessarily carries factors $\|A^{-1}\|^k$ or $\|B^{-1}\|^k$ (or a smallness hypothesis on $\|A-B\|$ relative to the smallest singular value); here these are forward-flow Jacobian norms, bounded in the paper only by $\sqrt{d}\,e^{\sqrt{d}\sqrt{q}\operatorname{Lip}_1^\Theta}$, not by $2$. No hypotheses are stated or verified, so the step is unsupported as written. The identical pattern recurs in lem:sub_gaussian and thm:concentration_bound.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Apply a correct log-determinant perturbation inequality carrying the inverse-Jacobian factors and bound those factors by the already-established forward-flow Jacobian estimates (e.g. $\|D\Phi^\theta\|\le\sqrt{d}e^{\sqrt{d}\sqrt{q}\operatorname{Lip}_1^\Theta}$); since $k\le d$, the factors are absorbed into the exponentials already present in the displays immediately following each invocation, so all stated bounds survive with their stated growth.
issues.overall_effect: The three log-determinant difference estimates, and hence the constants $\bar L$ and $D$ and the KL model-error bound, are not justified as written; transitively the generalization-error bounds and the PAC result in the main theorem inherit the gap.
issues.title: Determinant sensitivity bound invoked without invertibility/conditioning factors
issues.why_classification: The repair inserts standard conditioning factors that are already bounded in-context and absorbed into existing constants; no lemma, statement, rate, or guarantee changes.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Then the mappings $\theta \mapsto v_t^\theta(x) \otimes \eta_d(x)\quad \text{and} \quad \theta \mapsto D\left(v_t^\theta \otimes \eta_d \right)(x)$ are $\| \cdot\|_2-d_\Theta$ Lipschitz continuous, with constants

issues.failure_explanation: The proof bounds $\|D_x\tilde v^\theta(p,1-t)-D_x\tilde v^{\theta'}(q,1-t)\|$ with $p={[\Phi_t^\theta]}^{-1}(x)\ne q={[\Phi_t^{\theta'}]}^{-1}(x)$ (the two backward trajectories, which the lemma itself shows differ) by $\operatorname{Lip}_1^\Theta\|\theta-\theta'\|$. But Lemma lem:lip_constants controls $\theta\mapsto D(v_t^\theta\otimes\eta_d)(x)$ only at a fixed evaluation point; neither it nor Corollary cor:c1_bound provides the spatial Lipschitz constant of $D_x(v^\theta\otimes\eta_d)$ — a second-derivative-type bound for bounded-weight ReQU networks — needed to bridge the two distinct points. Hence the increments $Z_{\theta,n}-Z_{\theta',n}$ are not shown to be sub-Gaussian with proxy $\frac{\bar L^2}{n}d_\Theta^2(\theta,\theta')$, the property to which Dudley's entropy integral is applied. (The same point-mismatch arises in thm:learnability_target_class, but there the missing ingredient follows from the smoothness of $u^\mu$; here it must be derived for the network class.)
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Establish a new lemma bounding, uniformly over $\theta\in[-1,1]^q$, the spatial Lipschitz constant of $D_x(v^\theta\otimes\eta_d)$ on $[0,1]^{d+1}$ in terms of $(L,W,d)$ (bounded-weight ReQU networks are $C^{1,1}$ with such bounds, analogous to the estimates of Lemmas 3.2/3.7 of ehrhardt2025); combine it with the Gronwall trajectory bound already derived to control the mixed difference by $(\operatorname{Lip}_1^\Theta+G\,e^{\sqrt d\sqrt q\operatorname{Lip}_1^\Theta}\operatorname{Lip}_0^\Theta)\|\theta-\theta'\|$ and enlarge $\bar L$. The new term is of $\operatorname{Lip}_0$-type, so the growth bound of Remark rmk:main_constant_L and all downstream results survive with adjusted constants.
issues.overall_effect: The sub-Gaussianity claim and the constant $\bar L$ of lem:sub_gaussian are unproven as written; consequently thm:dudley, thm:concentration_bound, and the PAC-learnability result thm:learnability_sparse_grid are not established.
issues.title: Sub-Gaussian increment bound misapplies the parameter-Lipschitz estimate across different trajectory points
issues.why_classification: The repair needs a new, contained but nontrivial lemma (a uniform second-derivative bound for ReQU networks) plus a rederivation of the sub-Gaussian proxy, which exceeds a routine local fix; however, no global proof architecture changes and no stated guarantee, regime, or rate is lost.

issues.failure_explanation: By definition $\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm{gen}}=\sup_\theta|Z_{\theta,n}|$, whereas Dudley's inequality is applied to $\mathbb{E}[\sup_\theta Z_{\theta,n}]$; the asserted equality is false in general (e.g. if $Z_{\theta,n}<0$ for all $\theta$ then $\sup_\theta Z_{\theta,n}<0<\sup_\theta|Z_{\theta,n}|$). The correct comparison gives $\mathbb{E}[\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm{gen}}]\le2\,\mathbb{E}[\sup_\theta Z_{\theta,n}]$, bounding $\sup_\theta(-Z_{\theta,n})$ by the same Dudley argument; in addition, the substitution $\int_0^{2\sqrt q}\sqrt{q\log(1+2\sqrt q/\varepsilon)}\,d\varepsilon=2q\int_0^1\sqrt{\log(1+2/u)}\,du$ drops a further factor of $2$. Hence the constant $48$ in thm:dudley is not established by the proof.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the equality by $\mathbb{E}[\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm{gen}}]\le2\,\mathbb{E}[\sup_\theta Z_{\theta,n}]$, bound $\sup_\theta(-Z_{\theta,n})$ with the same Dudley argument, and repair the factor $2$ in the covering-number substitution; the constant $48$ becomes $96$ (up to equivalent bookkeeping) and all downstream statements hold with adjusted constants.
issues.overall_effect: The numerical constant in thm:dudley, and with it the constants in thm:concentration_bound and in the explicit thresholds of the main theorem's proof, are unjustified as written; the form, order, and dependence structure of all bounds survive.
issues.title: Dudley step equates the expected supremum of absolute increments with the supremum
issues.why_classification: Only constant-level bookkeeping in the proofs changes; every statement survives with an $O(1)$ larger constant and no guarantee, rate, or scope is affected.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof of the main theorem restates the risk decomposition without the factor $2$ on the generalization error, contradicting the paper's own decomposition, which carries it. The standard ERM argument needs uniform deviation control at both $\hat\theta_n$ and the model-optimal parameter, so the factor cannot be dropped in general. Consequently the derived generalization-error threshold $\varepsilon^2/(16\|Q\|_\infty^2)$ and the constants in the subsequent probability bound and sample-size threshold are unjustified; with the correct decomposition the threshold becomes $\varepsilon^2/(32\|Q\|_\infty^2)$ given the model-error bound used.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use the decomposition with the factor $2$ and adjust the constants in the subsequent chain (the generalization-error threshold becomes $\varepsilon^2/(32\|Q\|_\infty^2)$); the conclusion of the theorem is unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: The explicit constants in the probability chain of the main theorem's proof are unreliable as written; the PAC-learnability statement of thm:learnability_sparse_grid itself survives with adjusted thresholds.
issues.title: Main proof drops the factor 2 in the empirical risk decomposition
issues.why_classification: A forced constant-level repair inside the proof; the theorem's statement, the existence of the thresholds, and all guarantees are preserved.
